claim_not_supported: That the reproduction is inferior to the accepted checkpoint. Nothing here shows that; the point estimate is one paired unit in 1,024 and seven of eight margins clear.
That the reproduction is non-inferior on vs-random EWR under the frozen rule. It is not certified, and the rule reads the bound, not the point estimate. This packet does not lower the margin.
That G1 passes. Under the frozen decision rule it does not, and the gate is recorded as failed rather than converted into telemetry.
observed_fact: The control ran the full 25,000 updates from the exact canonical fresh C1 initialization (checksum cfe60bb0...), consumed 6,399,705 examples - the same count as the accepted run - and exercised a real stop/restart at 12,500 through the accepted resume path.
All 42 original Phase 8 gates pass for the reproduction, and all 26 Agent 6 completion gates pass.

Re-measuring the accepted checkpoint through this wrapper reproduced its recorded results exactly: all ten headline metrics at delta 0.0, including the sealed-test head metrics to ten decimal places and both play EWRs and their bootstrap lower bounds.
Seven of the eight frozen paired margins are cleared on the deciding bound.
The eighth, vs-random EWR, has a point estimate of -0.000244 and a 95% interval of [-0.011963, +0.011230]; its lower bound misses the -0.01 margin.

The vs-random paired instrument's own resolution at its frozen 1,024 setup pairs is +/-0.011599, wider than the 0.010 margin it was asked to certify. The two arms disagree on 171 of 1,024 paired units.
The random-EWR point gate that P18-D001 flagged as fragile - cleared by the accepted result by only 1.511 SE - passed: 0.956543 against a 0.950 floor.
Zero non-finite outputs, zero illegal actions, zero model failures, zero missing cases, and no accepted artifact changed.
plausible_but_untested: That a replicate control would land on the other side of zero and clear the margin. Its interval would be about as wide, so the outcome would turn on the sign of a near-zero delta - which is why sampling until one passes would be illegitimate rather than informative.
That the 0.189 paired-difference standard deviation is characteristic of any two faithful Phase 8 reproductions. Only one reproduction exists, so this is one draw, not a distribution.
supported_inference: The accepted Phase 8 warmstart reproduces from a fresh canonical initialization. Every original gate passes and every head and play metric sits within a few thousandths of the accepted result.
The wrapper is a faithful instrument, not merely an asserted one: it reproduced the accepted checkpoint's published numbers exactly before the candidate was scored.

The single failing margin is a measurement-design deficit, not a strength deficit. Certifying a 0.010 margin at this delta needs 1,448 paired setups; the frozen bank holds 1,024. No amount of model quality closes that gap, because the width comes from game-level noise between two independently trained networks.

The margin set was not anchored on power. vs-init carries a looser margin (0.03) on half the pairs and clears comfortably, while vs-random carries a tighter margin (0.01) on twice the pairs and cannot be certified. The tightening was justified in the contract by gate headroom, which is a different quantity from the paired instrument's resolution.

notes_for_the_reviewing_chat: The margin that failed is the only one in the contract that was tightened relative to its sibling on headroom reasoning. Re-deriving 0.011599 from the arm artifacts is the single check most worth repeating independently: it is the difference between 'the reproduction is weaker' and 'the ruler is too short'.

This is the third time the project has set a margin without checking the instrument's resolution - after the Phase 16 shootout's 0.03 margin at 0.53 SE and Phase 17's 120-board lane at 0.1379 MDE. A standing rule that every predeclared margin ships with the n needed to certify it would have caught all three before the run rather than after.

The reference arm reproducing all ten accepted metrics at exactly 0.0 also says something the contract did not assume: the greedy evaluation path is bitwise reproducible on MPS. Only the 25,000-step training run carries the nondeterminism the contract warns about.

proposed_next_question.note_on_scope: Setup work remains unauthorized either way. Nothing in this packet bears on G2, and no setup code was written or run.
proposed_next_question.question: Is the vs-random non-inferiority margin certifiable at all with the frozen 1,024-pair evaluation bank, and if not, what margin should G1 be judged against - a power-anchored one, or one measured from a replicate pair of reproductions?
proposed_next_question.why_it_discriminates: It separates the two readings this packet cannot separate on its own. Either the reproduction is fine and the margin was mis-specified - in which case G1 closes once the margin is re-anchored on the instrument's measured resolution, before any new result is opened - or the operator wants a measured run-to-run distribution, in which case the authorized replicate supplies one point of it and the margin is set from evidence rather than judgement. Both routes are decided before a result is seen, which is what keeps the re-anchoring from being a threshold lowered after the fact.

question.alternative_hypothesis: all original Phase 8 gates pass and every required paired non-inferiority bound is on the accepted side of its frozen margin
question.bounded_question: Can the accepted Phase 8 warmstart be reproduced from a fresh canonical C1 initialization under the frozen Phase 8 contract, passing all 42 original gates and the predeclared paired non-inferiority comparison?
question.confidence_rule: 95% two-sided bootstrap, 10,000 replicates; the deciding bound, never the point estimate
question.null_hypothesis: the fresh Phase 8 reproduction is inferior to the accepted checkpoint on one or more frozen paired margins, or fails an original Phase 8 gate

practical_margins.basis: no replicate Phase 8 run exists, so these are predeclared judgments, not estimates from a measured run-to-run distribution; each is stated as an absolute allowance on the paired delta and each is small relative to the original gate headroom
practical_margins.decision_rule: non-inferiority holds when the 95% bootstrap bound on the paired delta lies on the non-inferior side of the margin; a point estimate alone never decides
practical_margins.headroom_note: belief_ce_ratio has the least headroom of the three head gates (accepted 0.9205 against a 0.98 maximum), which is why its margin is half the others'

predeclared_failure_interpretations.one_replicate: run ONE replicate control under the same frozen config to estimate run-to-run spread before concluding the reproduction failed; a single out-of-margin control with no replicate does not distinguish an implementation defect from MPS variance
predeclared_failure_interpretations.random_ewr_only: if the control fails ONLY this gate while (a) its paired bootstrap lower bound still exceeds 0.90, and (b) its paired delta against the accepted checkpoint satisfies vs_random_ewr_delta_min, the packet records a REPRODUCTION TOLERANCE EVENT, sets G1 to REVISE, and escalates to the operator. It is NOT recorded as a pass. This interpretation is fixed here, before any control result exists, and may not be widened afterwards.

question.primary_metric: the 42 original gates plus 8 paired non-inferiority bounds

replicate_authorization.authorized_by: instruction section C4, conditionally, to estimate MPS run-to-run variation
replicate_authorization.why_not: C4 authorizes the replicate to decide whether an out-of-margin delta is explained by run-to-run variation. The delta here is -0.000244, so there is no excursion for run-to-run variation to explain. The bound misses because the paired interval at 1,024 pairs is +/-0.011599 against a 0.010 margin, which is within-run game-level noise and is unchanged by running the training again. A replicate would cost a further sealed-test access on a split the contract asks to count and minimise, and would decide the gate on the sign of a near-zero delta. It remains available to the operator; it is declined here because it does not discriminate, not because it is unauthorized.

results.why_the_one_margin_failed: the vs-random paired instrument resolves +/-0.011599 at its frozen 1,024 setup pairs, and the predeclared margin is 0.010. The point estimate is -0.000244, one paired unit in 1,024. The bound misses because the margin was set 16% tighter than the evaluation can certify, not because the reproduction is weaker: certifying 0.010 at this delta needs 1,448 pairs and the frozen bank holds 1,024. The vs-init contrast, whose margin is looser (0.03) on half the pairs, clears with room. P18-D001 recorded in advance that these margins were predeclared judgments with no measured run-to-run distribution behind them; this is that gap becoming visible.
